Lambo's Revuelto SV Gets the Ad Personam Treatment, Looks Like an Exotic Pumpkin Late for Halloween
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | lamborghinimiami
Actually, it’s not late for Halloween, because images of this supercar were shared online before the holiday. We were just late to catch them. But better late than never, right?
First things first, let’s dedicate a few lines to the actual model, which is the latest and greatest Lambo that money can buy. It is called the Lamborghini Revuelto SV , with its suffix standing for SuperVeloce, and “veloce” is Italian for “speed,” in case you forgot. The company’s fastest and most powerful model ever debuted when it was still summer in the northern hemisphere, as it was unveiled in August during the 2026 Monterey Car Week.
This is the latest in a long line of SV models, which also included the SV versions of the Aventador, Murcielago, Diablo, and Miura. It features a revised suspension with manually-adjustable dampers that were derived from GT3 racing, and this move is said to have increased the agility and lateral grip by 17 and 10 percent, respectively over the regular Revuelto. It features center locking wheels, 20 inches at the front and 21 inches at the rear, backed up by new carbon ceramic brakes.
A new Integrated Brake Control System is also on deck, and the Lamborghini Revuelto SV features a unique front fascia with a more pronounced apron, as well as black accents, dry carbon fiber, and the dedicated SV livery. A rear gurney flap, a fixed rear wing, a sports exhaust system with matte gray tips, and others are also on deck. The model is said to generate 80 percent more downforce compared to the standard Revuelto, and 10 percent more than the old Aventador SVJ (not the SV).
Photo: Instagram | lamborghinimiami And if these aren’t enough to convince you that you are looking at a serious supercar, then you should know that there are also modifications on the inside. Here, the steering wheel has been revised, and the vehicle has been equipped with carbon fiber door panels. The carbon fiber shelled seats are standard, and full-on carbon fiber racing seats are available as an option.
Production of the Lamborghini Revuelto SV is limited to 1,963 units, and this is a highly-customizable model straight from the factory. Take the pictured example, for instance, which benefits from multiple goodies signed by Ad Personam. The Raging Bull’s personalization division says that more than 400 color shades are available, joined by “an extensive range of customization options” that “allow owners to create a Lamborghini that reflects their vision.”
This particular ride is presented in Arancio Egon Matt, which is complemented by the Bronzo Serse accents on the SV logo, rear diffuser, Lamborghini lettering, and others, and the Nero Noctis livery. The wheels sport a Bronze Diamond Cut look, and the brake calipers visible from behind them have the same look.
Opening the door will reveal the Nero Cosmus Corsa-Tex and Arancio Dryope leather upholstery, as well as the Bronzo Oreadi embroidery that also includes the SV logo. Bronzo contrast stitching is part of the special optional makeover , alongside the Bronzo Serse painted accents, and the matte carbon fiber trim on the center console.
Photo: Instagram | lamborghinimiami This bright orange Lamborghini Revuelto SV, with its black details, bronze accents, dry carbon trim, and other goodies is definitely something to write home about, especially if you are into modern-day supercars. The Benjamins haven’t been mentioned in the social media post from Lamborghini Miami, but then again, you didn’t think that the sum would be discussed, did you?
Nevertheless, this is one pricey cookie , as it is estimated to start at almost $750,000, and that’s before factoring in any options, let alone the Ad Personam goodies available for it. A fully-specced example can end up costing close to the six-digit territory. As for the regular Revuelto, it kicks off at over $600,000.
Lamborghini’s Revuelto SV is not only a lot more advanced than the standard Revuelto, but also boasts more oomph. The naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12 engine and the three axial flux electric motors, two at the front and one above the 8-speed DCT, work in concert to deliver a total of 1,050 hp (1,065 ps/783 kW). There is also a new 7.3 kWh battery pack on deck.
The Revuelto SV hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 2.4 seconds, and it is 0.1 seconds faster than the standard model. It also has 49 hp (50 ps/37 kW) more, though flat-out, it is a bit slower, as the top speed is 216 mph (348 kph) as opposed to 217 mph (350 kph) in the regular version of the brand’s new-gen flagship supercar.
It looks like Lamborghini is cooking up something more special for the Revuelto, because a mysterious tester was recently scooped in the open, and some believe that it could be the even more extreme SVJ. Guess we’ll have to wait and see if that is indeed the case or not. Meanwhile, what’s your take on this Ad Personam SV? Is it a yay o a yay?
